findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_catalog" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Full-text search the catalog by any mix of track / artist / album tokens. Use this to resolve a fuzzy, partial, or misspelled name into concrete tracks BEFORE c…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_audio_features · Private data: search_catalog · Public sink: suggest_next_track, get_recommendations, tag_track · Destructive: get_audio_features, find_compatible_keys, build_setlist, get_recommendations, get_related_artists.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_audio_features · Private data: search_catalog · Public sink: suggest_next_track, get_recommendations, tag_track · Destructive: get_audio_features, find_compatible_keys, build_setlist, get_recommendations, get_related_artists

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_audio_features" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
